summary.text:
• Baltimore County's NCR Trail is a popular destination for running, walking, biking, and tubing access.
• Gnome Hill, a unique and colorful landmark, sits less than one mile north of White Hall, Maryland, near the trail.
• Only one travel item was published in the last hour, and its description is cut off, so further details are unavailable.

Less than one mile north of the White Hall NCR Trail parking lot sits a small hill covered in gnomes, and gnome puns. The owner of the property estimates that Gnome Hill has been around for over 20 years, but says that it really gained momentum around 2020. items.description: A writer walks the Polish-Czech Friendship Trail, where during the Cold War, dissidents from the two countries met to discuss their efforts against Communism.

items.author: Gareth Roberts
items.description: As a new film about Sherpa Tenzing Norgay is released, we visit Pen-Y-Gwryd, the Snowdonia hotel that served as British ‘base camp’ for the 1953 expedition and where the spirit of adventure lives on In the early hours of 2 June 1953, guests at the Pen-Y-Gwryd hotel in the heart of Eryri (Snowdonia) were woken from their sleep by the sound of footsteps running down the corridor outside their rooms. The commotion was followed by gleeful shouting and the sound of champagne corks popping. A late-ni…

items.title: 5 Bike Ride Trails in the U.S. That You’ll Really Love
items.author: Lauren Matison
items.description: When we recently featured a few of the best car-free bike rides in America, readers had a lot of recommendations for trails we had missed. We picked five to share.

items.title: Winter warmers: 10 of Britain’s best heated lidos
items.author: Rachel Dixon
items.description: From an infinity pool with sauna in Scotland to a restored Victorian gem in Bristol, here are 10 great spots where you can swim in comfort year-round Portavadie, on the banks of Loch Fyne on the west coast of Scotland, was originally earmarked as an oil rig, but plans fell through. Today it is a marina with holiday homes, a restaurant and bar, a gift shop, and a leisure centre with what is believed to be the biggest heated outdoor infinity pool in Scotland. There are also outdoor spa pools and…

items.description: Here’s one fan’s guide to visiting some of the genre’s fabled filming locations, from “The Shining” to “Friday the 13th.”

items.title: Chef Daniel Boulud’s 5 Favorite Places in Lyon, France
items.author: Celeste Moure and Camille McOuat
items.description: The world-famous chef, who just opened his latest outpost in Manhattan, shares some places he loves in the French city he says “will always be home.”

items.title: Atlas Obscura’s Guide to America’s Most Haunted Cemeteries
items.author: Holyn Thigpen
items.description: It’s nice to imagine death as an endless deep sleep, but not everyone is so lucky. In cemeteries across the U.S., you’ll find souls whose final resting places are not, in fact, restful at all. Perhaps they died with scores unsettled or, perhaps, their graves were ravaged by greedy developers. Sometimes, heartbreak rendered them unable to move on peacefully; in other cases, they simply couldn’t resist the chance to toy with their living visitors. One thing is certain: These restless spirits can…

items.title: It All Comes Together in Chattanooga
items.author: Daniel McDermon
items.description: Chattanooga may be best known for its natural beauty, surrounded by mountains, valleys, and the Tennessee River. This charming Appalachian city is also home to annual music festivals like the IBMA World of Bluegrass and the 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival . The streets and venues fill with musicians and fans dedicated to upholding the traditions of bluegrass music. Chattanooga has always been a city of convergence. items.title: ‘It’s hard to imagine the fires of July’: a bike ride through the Cairngorms in Scotland
items.author: Ailsa Sheldon
items.description: Wildfires raged through the national park this summer, but much of the landscape remains untouched – and autumn is the perfect time to go In the Cairngorms national park, the bracken is changing from dark green to russet and umber. Birch leaves are lined with gold, while the Scots pines remain proudly green. Autumn is arriving with a little sigh of relief here, after a summer few will forget. The wildfire that began near Glenmore and Abernethy on 15 July burned more than 33 sq km (13 sq miles)…

items.title: Fine scenery, historic towns and great pubs: a weekend walk on the Shropshire Way
items.author: Jane Dunford
items.description: A new series of rambles cuts the 185-mile trail into bitesize portions reachable by train, with urban beavers, the Devil’s Chair tor and some delicious food along the way Few pubs boast a more idyllic setting. As I emerge from the woods after a 15-mile hike, The Bridges , on the banks of the Onny River, in the rolling south Shropshire hills, glistens in the late afternoon sun. items.author: Adam Turner
